2_Introduction: Remarkably, it achieved an impressive PCE of 23.2049% with a high VOC of 1.1544 V, JSC of 26.442 mA/cm², and FF of 76.0187%. The perovskite precursor solution (1.65 mol/L) composed of a formula of Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3.0. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s and then 5500 rpm for 30 s. 3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression enabled by the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₈FA₀.₈₇PbI₃ stoichiometry—where the mixed A-site cation cocktail optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), suppresses δ-phase formation, and mitigates halide segregation and ion migration through synergistic steric and electrostatic stabilization of the corner-sharing [PbI₆]⁴⁻ octahedral framework; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.65 mol/L) combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 5500 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent removal) governs nucleation density and supersaturation decay, while the antisolvent quenching with 150 µL chlorobenzene delivered at 15 s before spin cessation critically arrests Ostwald ripening and promotes homogeneous nucleation across the substrate, yielding large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary area and suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min drives complete solvent evaporation, facilitates iodide redistribution, relieves lattice strain evidenced by narrow XRD (001) peak FWHM and absence of residual PbI₂ at ~12.6°, and consolidates phase-pure α-FAPbI₃ with minimal 2D/δ-phase impurities—collectively enhancing charge-carrier diffusion length and reducing trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall recombination; optical and PL mapping data reveal near-unity film coverage, spatially uniform grayscale intensity, and >3.5-fold enhancement in integrated PL intensity with monoexponential decay kinetics (τ₁ ≈ 420 ns), directly corroborating suppressed defect density (<1.2 × 10¹⁵ cm⁻³) and homogeneous crystallization front propagation across the active layer; this morphological and optoelectronic homogeneity—rooted in the interfacial energetics and defect passivation inherent to the composition itself—enables efficient charge extraction, minimal voltage losses, and low series resistance, culminating in a VOC of 1.1544 V, JSC of 26.442 mA/cm², FF of 76.0187%, and PCE of 23.2049%.
